turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Hi, I'm going to grab a few numbers before the doctor comes in. Have a seat right here.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh sure, sure. The parking garage was a nightmare, we circled for like twenty minutes, and then the elevator smelled like someone spilled coffee in it.
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Mom, she doesn't need the parking story.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm just saying, my heart's probably racing from those stairs.
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): Blood pressure is one thirty-two over seventy-eight, pulse is eighty-two, and oxygen is ninety-seven percent. Temperature is ninety-eight point four, respirations sixteen.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Ninety-seven, that's pretty good, right? I used to check my dad's with that little finger clip.
[SEG0007] person_1 (NURSE): Those look fine for now. Dr. Shah will be right in.
[SEG0008] person_4 (DOCTOR): Good morning, I'm Dr. Shah. I see you brought someone with you.
[SEG0009] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'm her daughter, Priya. I drove her over.
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm Helen. Well, the reason I'm here is this cough. It will not quit. It's been six weeks, started right after I had the flu.
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): And the flu, oh my god, I was on the couch for days. I missed book club, and Janet brought soup that was way too salty, I still haven't told her.
[SEG0012] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The cough is the thing. It's worse at night. I can hear her from the guest room.
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, nights are the worst. Daytime I can mostly ignore it, unless I'm talking a lot, like now.
[SEG0014] person_4 (DOCTOR): So a cough for six weeks, came on after the flu, and it's worse at night. Did I get that right?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): That's it. You got it.
[SEG0016] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any fever with this now?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever. I checked a couple times because Priya made me. It was normal.
[SEG0018] person_4 (DOCTOR): Coughing up any blood?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): No, no blood. Just a little clear stuff in the morning, then it's dry the rest of the day.
[SEG0020] person_4 (DOCTOR): Short of breath at all?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): A little, if I go up the stairs. Not like I can't breathe.
[SEG0022] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She gets winded walking Biscuit, and that loop is flat.
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Biscuit pulls. He's a beagle mix, stubborn as anything. But yeah, I'm a bit more winded than I was.
[SEG0024] person_4 (DOCTOR): How about your weight? Any weight loss?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I haven't lost weight.
[SEG0026] person_4 (DOCTOR): Appetite okay?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm eating fine. We went to that Thai place Tuesday and I finished the whole pad see ew.
[SEG0028] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Mom, your jeans are practically falling off. You keep hiking them up.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Those jeans? I thought they stretched in the wash. Well, actually, um, they are loose. I had to go in a notch on the belt.
[SEG0030] person_4 (DOCTOR): So the clothes are looser, even though you didn't set out to lose weight.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): I guess so. I never got on a scale. I couldn't tell you when it started, a couple months, maybe longer, it's fuzzy.
[SEG0032] person_4 (DOCTOR): Night sweats? Waking up drenched?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I wake up from the cough, not because I'm sweaty.
[SEG0034] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): No chest pain.
[SEG0036] person_4 (DOCTOR): Have you traveled anywhere recently, out of the country or a long trip?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Nope. I've been home. Didn't even go to Janet's lake house, and she asked twice.
[SEG0038] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any contact with someone who has tuberculosis, or a cough that wouldn't go away?
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I don't know anyone like that.
[SEG0040] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): What about cousin Ray? He was in the hospital, and Uncle said they were worried it was TB.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): That wasn't TB. He had pneumonia, I think. And I hardly saw him.
[SEG0042] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): You stayed at their place three nights. They had a mask on his door.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): You're blowing it up. I don't remember it that way. Whenever it was, last winter or the one before, I honestly can't pin it down.
[SEG0044] person_4 (DOCTOR): Let me say the cough part back. Six weeks after a flu, worse at night, a little morning phlegm, and some shortness of breath on stairs and with the dog.
[SEG0045] person_4 (DOCTOR): No fever, no blood, no chest pain, no night sweats, no recent travel. You first said no weight loss, but the clothes are looser and you can't date it.
[SEG0046] person_4 (DOCTOR): There's also this question about cousin Ray, possible TB versus pneumonia, and the timing is unclear. I'm not going to put a name on the cause today.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. I appreciate you not jumping. My neighbor got told three different things in one week and she was a wreck.
[SEG0048] person_4 (DOCTOR): What medicines do you take?
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): Lisinopril, twenty milligrams, every morning, for my blood pressure. I've been on it for years.
[SEG0050] person_4 (DOCTOR): Anything else?
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): There's an orange pill for my cholesterol. I can never remember the name. Don't ask me the dose either, it's gone.
[SEG0052] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I looked in the bottle once. I want to say atorvastatin, but I might be mixing it up with Dad's old pills.
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): See, we don't actually know. I just take the orange one at night.
[SEG0054] person_4 (DOCTOR): All right, we'll leave that one unnamed. Did you take anything for the flu itself?
[SEG0055] person_2 (PATIENT): A Z-pack, azithromycin. I finished all five days. I'm not on it anymore.
[SEG0056] person_4 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke, or did you?
[SEG0057] person_2 (PATIENT): I quit eight years ago. Used to be a pack a day, back when everybody did. I don't miss it, except sometimes at a barbecue.
[SEG0058] person_4 (DOCTOR): I'm going to listen to your lungs now. Deep breaths for me.
[SEG0059] person_2 (PATIENT): This always makes me cough, sorry.
[SEG0060] person_4 (DOCTOR): Lungs are clear, no wheeze, no crackles. Heart's regular. Your throat looks a little red, nothing dramatic.
[SEG0061] person_2 (PATIENT): The throat's been scratchy off and on, I forgot to mention that. Not painful, just scratchy.
[SEG0062] person_4 (DOCTOR): Okay, scratchy throat too. My first thought was to skip pictures and try a budesonide inhaler for a couple of weeks, since a lot of post-flu coughs fade.
[SEG0063] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): With the weight thing and Ray, are you sure just waiting is smart?
[SEG0064] person_4 (DOCTOR): You're right to push on that. I'm changing the plan. No inhaler today. I am going to order a chest X-ray, and you can get it downstairs before you leave.
[SEG0065] person_2 (PATIENT): An X-ray. All right. Is that because you think it's something bad?
[SEG0066] person_4 (DOCTOR): I'm not naming a cause. I just want a look. If the X-ray doesn't explain it and the cough hasn't settled, we might do a CT later, but I'm not ordering that now.
[SEG0067] person_2 (PATIENT): CT sounds expensive. Does insurance even cover it? Never mind, Priya handles the paperwork, I lose every envelope.
[SEG0068] person_4 (DOCTOR): Let's see you back in two weeks with the result. If you cough up blood, spike a fever, or get short of breath just sitting, don't wait, go to the ER.
[SEG0069] person_1 (NURSE): I can send the X-ray order and walk you down to radiology when you're ready.

spec.situation: Cough for six weeks after flu; worse at night; patient says no weight loss, then says clothes are loose; recent travel or TB contact denied by patient but a family member recalls a cousin's illness; doctor orders chest X-ray, avoids naming a cause.
features: doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.
hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.
vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.
doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).

omissions.text: Cough is mostly dry for the rest of the day, with clear sputum only in the morning.
Negative finding: no known contact with someone who has tuberculosis or a cough that would not go away, per patient (despite later family disagreement about cousin Ray).

Weight loss history is recorded incompletely/wrongly: the patient initially denied weight loss, then acknowledged looser clothes and needing a tighter belt notch, without having weighed herself and without intending to lose weight.
Past history of influenza immediately before the cough began.
Planned budesonide inhaler trial for a couple of weeks was discussed as the initial plan, but then explicitly cancelled after reconsideration; no inhaler was prescribed.
Chest X-ray was to be done downstairs before the patient leaves, not just generally planned.
